messages:
elaine: quick follow-up to the rollout metadata rfc: i sketched a small, practical shape that keeps pin intent server-side but gives clients an ordered fallback list + an epoch for cache invalidation. want quick thoughts.

tom: drop the example pls, want to see runtime fields.

elaine: tiny example pasted below. intent: let runtime pick fast and let control-plane rotate candidates without complex client logic.

```json
{
  "artifact_id": "auth-encoder-4b",
  "stamp": "v2026-04-02",
  "stamp_seq": 2,
  "stamp_fingerprint": "sha256:abcd...",
  "candidates": [
    {"type":"hash","id":"sha256:1111","variant":"fp16","priority":0},
    {"type":"stamp","id":"v2026-03-29","variant":"int8","priority":1}
  ],
  "fallback_policy": "ordered",
  "preferred_seq_len": 512,
  "stamp_origin": "auto-migration"
}
```

rene: +1 on stamp_seq and fingerprint. couple notes: (1) require clients to compare stamp_seq and re-resolve if control-plane seq > local, (2) control-plane should alert on fingerprint diffs but not auto-block by default, (3) dedicated tenants can opt into hard_pin in tenant_overrides.

tom: agree. also standardize that top-level preferred_seq_len is the fast-path used by placement. duplicate in client_hints only for backcompat.

ops-bot: schema-check: staging flagged mixed-type client_hints in previous builds; opened INF-4042.

elaine: action items: elaine will add stamp_seq + fingerprint + tenant_override blurb to appendix (ETA today). tom will confirm placement reads preferred_seq_len top-level (ETA tomorrow). rene will draft alert rule for fingerprint divergence and hook INF-4042 (ETA 2 days).

tom: sounds good. if no objections merge appendix after elaine updates. :thumbsup:
